farraa:1-1.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنفَطَرَتْ﴾: it was split.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ﴾.
What is in its belly of gold and silver came out, and the dead came out after that. It is one of the portents of the Hour that the earth brings out the pieces of its liver (أفلاذ كبدها), of its gold and its silver. Al-Farrāʾ said: الأفلاذ are pieces of liver cut lengthwise, المشرّح and المشرّحة; the singular is فِلْذ and فِلْذة.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ﴾ of its deeds ﴿وَأَخَّرَتْ﴾.
And what it left behind: whatever practice (sunna), good or evil, it established which was then acted upon.
The response (jawāb) to ﴿إذا السَّماء انفطَرتْ﴾ (1) is His saying: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ﴾.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it: "فَعَدَلَك", lightened, and the people of the Hijaz read it: "فعدَّلك", with shadda. Whoever reads it lightened, its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is: He turned you into whatever form He willed: either handsome or ugly, or tall or short.
He said: [al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying]: One of the shaykhs narrated to me from Layth from Ibn Abī Najīḥ that he said: in the form of a paternal uncle, in the form of a father, in the form of one of the relatives, by resemblance.
Whoever reads "فعدَّلك" with shadda means — and Allah knows best —: He made you well-proportioned, of balanced make. That is the more pleasing of the two to me and the better of them in Arabic, because you say: ﴿فى أى صورة ما شاء ركبك﴾ (in whatever form He willed He assembled you), so making في belong to the assembling (التركيب) is stronger in Arabic than making في belong to العدل (turning); [130/b] because saying عدلتك إلى كذا وكذا (I turned you to such and such) and صرفتك إلى كذا وكذا is better than saying عدلتك فيه and صرفتك فيه.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَلاَّ بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِٱلدِّينِ﴾.
With tāʾ. Some of the people of Medina read it with yāʾ, and some of them with tāʾ; al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim with tāʾ. The tāʾ is the better of the two because of His saying: "وإِنَّ عَلَيكُم" — He did not say: عليهم.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَآئِبِينَ﴾.
He says: once they enter it, they will not be brought out of it. The readers agreed on the accusative in ﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ﴾ (19), and the nominative would be permissible if it were read so. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that the Arabs prefer the nominative when they annex اليوم to يفعل, تفعل, أفعل and نفعل, saying: هذا يومُ نفعلُ ذاك (this is the day we do that), and أفعل ذاك, and نفعل ذاك. But when they say هذا يومَ فعلتَ, annexing يوم to فعلتُ or to إذ, they prefer the accusative. They recited to us:
عَلى حينَ عاتبْتُ المشيبَ على الصِّبا * وقُلتُ أَلَمَّا تَصْحُ والشَّيبُ وازِعُ؟
(At the time when I reproached grey hair for [the loss of] youth, and said: Have you not yet sobered up, when grey hair is a restrainer?)
With the yāʾ and tāʾ [forms] what is permissible with فعلت is also permissible; but most common is what al-Kisāʾī explained.
